package_info.package_manager: standalone binary (Go-based, distributed via PHP downloader scripts)
package_info.package_versions: Observed samples from Sep 2022 to Nov 2022 (e.g., SHA-256: c33e50c3be111c1401037cb42a0596a123347d5700cee8c42b2bd30cdf6b3be3)
package_info.why_malicious: GoTrim is a botnet malware that brute-forces WordPress and OpenCart sites, exfiltrates valid credentials to a C2 server, and enables remote control of compromised systems. It is distributed via malicious PHP scripts, deletes itself after execution to evade detection, and uses encrypted C2 communication to coordinate attacks and evade analysis.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon execution of the GoTrim binary)
execution_context.file_location: GoTrim main binary (ELF executable, Go language)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Upon execution, GoTrim generates a unique bot ID using the victim's external IP, HTTP server port, outbound IP, and a hardcoded AES passphrase, then sends an encrypted beacon request to the C2 server with victim and bot information.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code collects system/network identifiers, generates a unique bot ID, encrypts this data with AES-GCM, and sends it via HTTP POST to the C2 server, registering the victim and enabling remote tasking.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware should not collect and exfiltrate system/network identifiers to an external server, especially with encryption and unique bot IDs.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not fingerprint hosts and send this data to unknown remote servers on execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise management agents may register with a central server, but with user/admin consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Collection of external and internal IP addresses
Use of hardcoded encryption keys for C2 comms

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial beaconing, in client or server mode)
execution_context.file_location: GoTrim main binary (ELF executable, Go language)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: GoTrim receives AES-GCM encrypted commands from the C2 server (e.g., brute force tasks, target lists, credentials), decrypts them, and executes the specified attack (e.g., brute-forcing WordPress logins).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code receives encrypted tasking from the C2, parses target lists and credentials, and initiates brute-force attacks against specified CMS targets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Receiving and executing remote commands to attack third-party systems is a hallmark of botnet malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not accept encrypted remote instructions to attack other systems.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may receive commands, but not to attack external sites.

execution_context.file_location: GoTrim main binary (ELF executable, Go language)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: For each target, GoTrim attempts to enumerate WordPress usernames via GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users, then sends POST requests to /wp-login.php or uses XML-RPC to attempt logins with provided credentials.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During runtime, the code enumerates usernames from WordPress REST API, then attempts brute-force logins using POST or XML-RPC, reporting successful credentials to the C2.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated credential stuffing and brute-force attacks are malicious, especially when targeting thousands of domains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not attempt mass login attempts against unrelated third-party sites.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing tools may perform similar actions, but only with explicit authorization.

execution_context.file_location: GoTrim main binary (ELF executable, Go language)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Upon successful login, GoTrim updates a global status message with the target URL, username, password, command ID, and brute force status, then sends this data to the C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after a successful brute-force, the code exfiltrates valid credentials and attack metadata to the C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating valid credentials to a remote server is a clear sign of credential theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not send third-party credentials to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; credential exfiltration is always malicious.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when deployed via PHP script on compromised site)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PHP script downloads GoTrim binary from a hardcoded URL, saves it to the local directory, executes it, and then deletes both itself and the GoTrim binary.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the PHP script downloads and executes the GoTrim malware, then deletes itself and the binary to evade detection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated download and execution of a binary from an untrusted source, followed by self-deletion, is a classic malware dropper pattern.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PHP scripts do not download and execute binaries, nor do they delete themselves after execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate installers may clean up after themselves, but not in this context.

attack_chain.action: PHP downloader script is deployed on a compromised web server and executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: GoTrim binary is downloaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: GoTrim binary executes, fingerprints the host, generates a unique bot ID, and sends an encrypted beacon to the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Bot is registered with the C2 and awaits further instructions.

attack_chain.action: GoTrim receives encrypted commands from the C2 server, including brute-force tasks and target lists.
attack_chain.leads_to: Bot begins brute-force attacks against specified CMS targets.

attack_chain.action: GoTrim performs brute-force attacks against WordPress and OpenCart sites, attempting to enumerate usernames and log in with provided credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: If successful, valid credentials are obtained.

attack_chain.action: GoTrim exfiltrates successful credentials and attack metadata to the C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: C2 operators receive credentials for further exploitation.

attack_chain.action: PHP downloader and GoTrim binary delete themselves from the infected system to evade detection.

behavioral_signatures: Go-based binaries making encrypted HTTP POST requests to suspicious URLs
Automated brute-force login attempts against WordPress/OpenCart endpoints
Self-deleting PHP scripts that download and execute binaries
file_indicators: Presence of PHP scripts that download from hardcoded URLs and execute binaries
GoTrim ELF binaries (UPX-packed, ~1.9MB) in web server directories
Temporary files matching GoTrim sample hashes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PHP scripts that download and execute binaries from hardcoded URLs, especially those that self-delete. Detect Go-based binaries making encrypted HTTP POST requests to known C2 endpoints or using suspicious URL patterns. Look for automated brute-force activity against WordPress/OpenCart endpoints, especially with user enumeration via /wp-json/wp/v2/users. Correlate file creation and deletion events for evidence of self-cleaning malware. Use network monitoring to flag outbound connections to known C2 IPs and URLs.
